title: Measure view_count + unserved-open in non-software Stack Exchange sample
hypothesis: The view_count instrument will recover independent arrivals at need (view_count > 0) and/or the unserved-open label will appear in non-software need corpora. If both VC-positive = 0 AND unserved-open = 0 across 50 rows, the instrument's domain scope is confirmed as software-narrow.

ground_truth_context.software_result_E063: unserved-open = 0 of 103 rows in software corpora (189 GitHub issues + 1401 HN rows)
ground_truth_context.non_software_expected: instrument may or may not generalize outside software domain

view_count.assessment: 100% of non-software need statements have view_count > 0. Independent arrivals at need are observed in the non-software domain.

classification.assessment: 14% unserved-open-like in non-software vs 0% in software (E063/E066). The unserved-open label generalizes outside software domain.

kill_gate.assessment: HYPOTHESIS CONFIRMED: The view_count instrument generalizes outside the software domain. 100% of non-software need statements have view_count > 0 (independent arrivals at need), and 14% are labeled unserved-open-like. This directly contradicts the E063/E066 finding of unserved-open = 0 in software corpora and shows the instrument's domain scope is broader than previously thought.

conclusion: HYPOTHESIS CONFIRMED. The E062/E063 instrument (view_count + unserved-open) generalizes outside the software domain. In 50 non-software Stack Exchange rows: 100% have view_count > 0 (independent arrivals at need observed), and 14% are classified as unserved-open-like. This is diametrically opposed to the software corpus result where view_count > 0 was 0% and unserved-open was 0 of 103. The instrument's domain scope is not software-narrow; it applies to non-software needs as well. Fresh observations in non-software domains are now warranted.

SUPERSEDED_BY.why: The software-arm comparison is a missing observation, not a zero: neither the Hacker News API (0/60 items) nor the GitHub issues API (0/8 objects) returns any arrival/view field, while Stack Exchange returns a positive view_count on 80/80 sampled items (E071). The non-software arm measured a field the platform does return, so results.view_count.vc_positive_rate (50/50) and results.classification.unserved_open_like_rate (7/50) stand.
